programmes.t: George Clarke's Old House New Home
programmes.d: Anthony and Emily turn their ramshackle 17th-century cottage into a family home.
Chris Beardshaw's garden is transported from the Chelsea Flower Show to Great Ormond Street Hospital.
The team is tasked with building a new center for a charity that helps children with life-limiting conditions.
The team help a lady who suffers from brain damage, speech loss and paralysis after a stroke.
The team builds an entirely bespoke five-bedroom home for an inspirational family with complex special needs.
The team builds Sascha a home-dialysis room, which offers her a lifeline and extra years with her family.
The team helps a 12-year-old return home from the hospital for the first time in three years.
The story begins in the late 18th century when the building first came into royal hands.
From the tragic end of George III's time to the palace-loving teenage Queen Victoria.
1845 was a happy time at the palace for Victoria, Albert and their expanding family.
Buckingham Palace witnesses the triumphant - and tragic - final days of the Victorian era.
George V arrives on the throne and the iconic House of Windsor is born.
Buckingham Palace survives WWII and we arrive in the modern era of Queen Elizabeth II.
The castle soon became a weapon with which unruly barons challenged the crown.
The story of Edward I, who turned the castle into an instrument of colonization.
How castle ruins took on a unique appeal, embodying a nostalgia for an age of chivalry.
Dan Cruickshank reveals the buildings which cemented the monarch's claim to the throne.
A new style emerged as monarchs demanded that architecture proclaim their right to rule.
We go behind the imposing iron gates of the Royal Family's favorite holiday home.
The death of Edward VII in 1910 rocks Sandringham and the royals.
In 1952, tragedy struck as King George VI died suddenly in his sleep.
Fiona Bruce visits Buckingham Palace and learns of its long history.
Fiona Bruce visits Windsor Castle, the world's oldest and largest inhabited castle.
Fiona Bruce visits one of Britain's smallest palaces, Edinburgh's Palace of Holyroodhouse.
A look at South Africa's Blue Train, the Golden Eagle in Russia, and the Presidential Train in Portugal.
See why it's not the price tag that makes these extravagant vessels exceptional.
